previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and a history of anxiety was readmitted two days after discharge for recurrent nausea and vomiting. She presented with hypertensive crisis (BP 194/94) and lactic acidosis due to volume depletion, both of which improved with IV fluids and antihypertensive therapy. Throughout the hospitalization, she was observed inducing vomiting, leading to the recognition that her symptoms were primarily driven by a psychiatric condition. After discussions with GI and psychiatry, she acknowledged the psychological basis of her vomiting and committed to outpatient follow-up. Her diet was advanced, medications were optimized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for ongoing mental health support.
problems: Gastrointestinal malfunction arising from mental factors

Personal history of infections of the central nervous system

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms ___ was admitted for DKA and dehydration secondary to 
nausea and vomiting due to gastroparesis. Her DKA corrected with 
administration of insulin and IVF in the ED and her anion gap 
resolved.  She was admitted to the medical for for symptoms of 
nausea/inability to tolerate po thought to be secondary to her 
gastroparesis.  Her nausea continued on the floor and so she was 
started on ativan, compazine, zofran and her home 
metoclopromide. She was continued on IVF due to ongoing 
tachycardia 100-120s. Her tachycardia (which had been noted on 
previous admissions for gastroparesis) has been worked up 
extensively previously with no clear source, and no new 
concerning signs or symptoms noted during this hospitalization 
(previous hyperthyroid w/u negative, no signs infection, PE).  
The remainder of her vital signs remained noraml throughout.
.
She has had 30 admissions in ___ years for vomiting, ~3 day 
hospital course (with extensive workup and suggestion of J or G 
tube placement declined by pt because she recognizes that their 
is a psychiatric component) Psych consult on previous admission 
has suggested this is cyclic vomiting or rumination syndrome. 
She denies self-inducing vomiting when she is not nauseous. 
During her hospital course, it was noted that she was self 
inducing almost all of the vomiting reported, and therefore it 
was difficult to establish whether she was unable to tolerate PO 
due to her nausea.  Outpt psychiatry and scheduling an outpt 
therapist appointment was declined by the patient, was seen by 
inpt social work.  In speaking with the pt and her husband, they 
both agreed that stress and anxiety plays a large role in her 
admissions, and pt agreed to see psychologist at ___.  On 
discharge, the patient was tolerating soft diet, reported 
improved nausea and was not inducing vomiting.
